# Reading the life stages {.unnumbered}

What a body needs shifts predictably across the life course, from newborn to older adult. The six
chapters that follow are in life-course order, and each stage is described in terms of the same two sets of factors.
The **internal factors** are what changes inside the body: growth, hormones and physiology. The
**external factors** are what changes outside it: the food environment, activity, and who a person eats
with. Each stage is then examined for the needs that result, and for the point at which a normal shift has
become a problem that needs action.

One approach runs through all six chapters: **recognise and refer**. For now the task is to anticipate
the main nutritional need of each stage, recognise the red flag, advise what is simple and safe, and refer. Taking a
full diet history and appraising a trial are taught later, in Part III,
*Assessing and Advising Patients*, in the chapters on reading a healthy pattern, weighing the evidence,
assessing a diet and counselling for change. When a life-stage topic needs one of those skills, the
skill is left to its Part III chapter. Designing a therapeutic plan is left to the dietitian (see the
*Interprofessional practice, referral and looking after yourself* chapter).
